purpose: Native evidence for the five alarm/wave/scan action rows: forge.action.map.{alarm_start,alarm_stop,scan_start,wave_start,wave_stop}. Every hook signature, RVA and field layout below is read from the QA-profile interop assembly and the build 20403457 dump; every call edge is read out of GameAssembly.dll's own code section and is marked as a static scan, not as a game-verified observation.
gameVerifiedNote: No claim in this file was observed in a running game. The call edges were recovered by scanning the native code section for direct relative calls into the named method bodies; a call whose target lands on a jump stub, a virtual dispatch or an indirect call is not visible to that scan and is not claimed. Each such gap is stated per entry.
gameAssemblySha256: see objective-hooks.json (same build and same assembly)
rules: A write must go through the entry the game itself runs on the host and replicates; a private field write is not a write path.

An interop wrapper is public even when the native member is private (Il2CppInterop calls it through il2cpp_runtime_invoke), so 'callable' is not evidence of 'intended'; each entry below says which native caller exists.
A call edge recovered by byte scan is a hypothesis with a stated method; nothing here claims behaviour that was not read from the code.

types.note: The one native instance kind behind both the alarm and the scan; the author's reference is a ChainedPuzzleDataBlock and the runtime identity is this component.
The level's own puzzle list. `m_instances` is a field in the dump (no RVA) and is exposed by the interop as a public property.
The wave system's host-side owner; its event list is the wave registry.
The only subclass of Mastermind.MastermindEvent in this build, so every live event is a wave.

stateShapes.note: The replicator is what makes AttemptInteract a sync entry: the interaction goes in, the state callback comes out.
The interaction carries the enum and nothing else, which is why the request has no room for a per-request parameter.

stateVocabulary.note: Read from the interop enum file, which is decompiled from the interop assembly and matches the game's own order.
Carried by objective-hooks.json; the values are the ones the status transitions of OnStateChange compare.

identity.authorReference: GameData.ChainedPuzzleDataBlock: the game's own alarm/scan data block, whose PublicAlarmName is the author-facing name and whose TriggerAlarmOnActivate says whether the block is an alarm or a scan
identity.resourceIdConvention: This provider publishes the instance's own m_puzzleUID (assigned by the instance while it is set up, one counter per instance) and also resolves the data block's PublicAlarmName, so an author may address an alarm by either spelling. The convention is this slice's own decision and is not a native id: the evidence does not establish that PublicAlarmName is unique in a level, so both keys are matched and a resourceId that names two live instances resolves to neither.
identity.invalidatedBy: ChainedPuzzleInstance.OnDestroy (the object leaves the manager's list)
identity.unproven: the exact format of m_puzzleUID is not established; nothing here depends on its format, only on its being non-empty and per-instance

identity.authorReference: the pair (GameData.SurvivalWaveSettingsDataBlock.persistentID, GameData.SurvivalWavePopulationDataBlock.persistentID) — the two ids Mastermind.TriggerSurvivalWave takes
identity.runtimeInstance: the Mastermind event the start entry registers: Mastermind.MastermindEvent.EventID (ushort) on a SurvivalWave object
identity.resourceIdConvention: `<settingsId>:<populationId>`, the order the native entry takes the two ids in; it is the provider's own spelling of the author pair and is written into the plan as the compiled resource id
identity.note: A wave resource is a definition, not a running wave: the same resource can be started more than once and each start registers its own EventID. The running instance is therefore a handle, which is why wave_stop takes a handle and not this resource.

readbacks.note: The level's puzzle registry; every resolution of a chained-puzzle resource starts here and a level with no manager refuses with `chained-puzzle-manager-unavailable`.
Read by enumeration and by every action's resolution; the game adds a puzzle to this list while it builds the level.
The instance's own id, which this provider publishes as the resourceId of a chained-puzzle resource. Its format is not established and nothing here depends on it.
Read by alarm_start/scan_start to answer 'the state the request asked for already holds' without writing.
Read to refuse an alarm the game already solved, which is terminal for that instance.
The data block behind the instance, which is where the author alarm name is read.
A puzzle with no core cannot be activated by the game; the action refuses it by name rather than calling into it.

Resolves a running wave from the ushort EventID that pChainedPuzzleState and pSurvivalWaveSpawnData already carry. This is the lookup a handle-resolved wave_stop would use; the action layer does not call it while the handle table is missing.
The wave system's singleton; a level without it refuses with `wave-mastermind-unavailable`.

The level's own course node list. wave_start passes the first node it holds, because the row carries no position, no entity and no node of its own and the native entry requires one; a level with no node refuses with `wave-course-node-unavailable`.
The author settings block a wave resource names; a wave whose block this build did not load is refused as `resource-unavailable` rather than handed to the master.
The author population block a wave resource names, validated the same way as the settings block.
The wave resource provider's enumeration source, together with the population block's own GetAllBlocks; a wave is a definition the author loaded, not a running instance.

writes.role: the puzzle's own interaction entry and the only member a Forge alarm/scan request writes through. It hands the interaction to the instance's own state replicator (InteractWithState), whose provider callback is OnStateChange, so the master side of an activation runs where the game already runs it. `Activate` is alarm_start and scan_start; `Deactivate` is the single-instance stop an alarm_stop would issue once its handle resolves.

the host's wave start and the only member a wave_start writes through. It answers whether it accepted the wave and hands back the EventID it registered, which the wave facts and a handle-resolved wave_stop both name. The request's budget, count, seed and interval are not arguments of it: they are fields of the author's SurvivalWaveSettingsDataBlock or of the level, so a request naming one is refused rather than run without it.

readbacksAlarmWave: the rows above are the reads of this slice; the two writes are in `writes`
unproven: Whether MasterDeactivate publishes a new pChainedPuzzleState (and therefore replicates) was not established; the body contains no call into the state replicator that this scan found, and the class's push into the replicator was only found inside AttemptInteract. alarm_stop does not rely on it and is unimplemented for that reason.

The bodies of MasterActivate and MasterDeactivate were scanned for direct calls only; an indirect call, a virtual dispatch or a call through a function pointer inside them is invisible to that method.
The frequency of ChainedPuzzleManager.CreatePuzzleInstance was not measured, so no provider polls its list; both the resource enumeration and every action read it on demand.
PublicAlarmName uniqueness inside a level is not established.

Whether the alarm puzzle's own wave is registered against the objective manager for every author entry point is not established; RegisterSurvivalWaveID is called from Mastermind.TriggerSurvivalWave (callEdges mastermind-wave-node.calls-register-wave-id), and the puzzle's TriggerEnemyWave reaches the master by a path this slice did not trace to the end.
catalogMismatches: forge.action.map.wave_start declares budget/count/seed/interval inputs, but the only interop-visible native start entry takes neither a budget, a count, a seed nor an interval: the population budget and the group cadence are fields of the author's SurvivalWaveSettingsDataBlock, and the seed is the level's own. A request that carries one of the four is refused with `wave-knob-unsupported` rather than run without it.

forge.action.map.scan_start declares an `anchor` (vector3) and a `quorum` (integer). No native entry takes either: a puzzle is created at a position (ChainedPuzzleManager.CreatePuzzleInstance), an existing puzzle cannot be moved per request, and the number of players a scan requires is a field of its own data block (read by CP_Bioscan_Core). The anchor is therefore not applied and the quorum is echoed back in the result row, never written.

forge.action.map.alarm_stop declares `existing_enemies_policy` with `keep` and `clear`. Nothing native takes that decision: whether the wave started by the puzzle survives the puzzle's end is the data block's own DisableSurvivalWaveOnComplete, and clearing already-spawned enemies would be a second, Forge-owned enemy deletion path. `clear` is refused with `alarm-clear-unsupported`.

forge.action.map.wave_stop declares `pending_spawns_policy` with `cancel` and `finish`. The native stop removes the event, which is `cancel`; no entry lets a wave spend its remaining budget first, so `finish` is refused with `wave-pending-finish-unsupported`.

forge.action.map.wave_start and wave_stop are recorded in rows.tsv as belonging to ForgeEnemy (ruling 83: wave facts and wave control are the enemy package's), while this slice's specification names ForgeMap files. The declaration is written so the wave half can be moved without touching a native hook; the integration batch has to decide which package registers it.

The catalog's alarm_start/scan_start declare a `handle` output (alarm_handle/scan_handle) and the two stop rows declare a handle input. This runtime has no entry point that mints a provider handle and no table that turns one back into a native object, so the start rows publish their result only and the stop rows refuse with `handle-native-unavailable`.

integrationNotes: The integration batch must add `ResourceProviders` for the two kinds this slice declares (`chained-puzzle`, `wave`). Without a registered owner of a kind, a plan that carries a compiled resource reference of that kind is refused at load with `stale-resource` (RuntimePlan.ResolveResourceLiteral reads the registry's static declaration), so the two start rows cannot be driven end-to-end until the provider is registered.
The chained-puzzle provider belongs to whichever package owns the puzzle instance table; this slice publishes it from ForgeMap because the alarm and scan rows are declared there.
The plan ABI reads a resource port's value as {"resourceKind","resourceId"} and the kernel validates the kind against the port's own declaration, so the handler never has to guess a kind.
